title: Expose Philox RNG state reservation to Python as Generator.philox_state
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* #191020
* __->__ #191019

Python-authored CUDA kernels (e.g. the DSL overrides in torch/_native) need
to implement RNG ops that draw from the same Philox stream as aten's eager
kernels: reserve a chunk of the stream, get (seed, offset), advance the
generator. That primitive exists in C++ as
CUDAGeneratorImpl::philox_cuda_state(increment) but has no Python exposure;
the closest is the inductor-private inductor_reserve_rng_state dispatcher op.

Generator.philox_state(increment) returns (seed, offset, intragraph) as
three 1-element int64 tensors and mirrors the C++ PhiloxCudaState protocol
exactly: outside capture (HostState) seed/offset are CPU tensors holding
the current values, so callers pass them as scalar kernel arguments with no
device traffic; during capture (DevState) they are CUDA aliases of the
generator's per-capture extragraph tensors, which replay_prologue refills
on every replay, so kernels load them from device memory at run time.
Callers branch on capture state exactly like the built-in kernels branch on
PhiloxCudaState via at::cuda::philox::unpack. The extragraph storage is
made non-resizable so a caller cannot reallocate it out from under a
captured graph. Kernels consume (seed, offset + intragraph); reservation
semantics (increment rounded up to a multiple of 4, offset % 4 invariant)
match every other philox_cuda_state caller.

The name is device-generic (not philox_cuda_state) since the contract is
about the Philox engine, not CUDA: non-Philox generators raise
NotImplementedError from the c10 default.

The c10::GeneratorImpl virtual follows the TensorImpl.h pattern for
at::Tensor in c10 interfaces: forward-declared at::Tensor out-params (a
by-value at::Tensor cannot be returned from a function defined in c10,
where the type is incomplete); at::Generator::philox_state returns the
tuple. No TensorImpl/intrusive_ptr handling outside the impl boundary.

The API is public and documented (torch/_torch_docs.py), including the
exact reservation contract (fixed seed, owned counter range, all
subsequences, curand parameter mapping), the HostState/DevState return
modes and graph-capture aliasing/lifetime contract, the int64
reinterpretation of the uint64 seed and offset, and the modulo-2**64
offset wrap.

Authored with Claude Code.

Test Plan:

New tests in test/test_cuda.py: eager reservation values, CPU return
devices, and offset advancement, increment rounding, reproducibility of a
reservation via set_offset, seed/offset int64-reinterpretation at >= 2**63
including uint64 offset wraparound, error cases, shared graphsafe state,
and graph capture/replay including non-resizability of the returned
aliases.

```
python test/test_cuda.py -k philox_state -v
python test/test_cuda.py -k graphsafe -v
```

+/**
+ * Tensor-based variant of philox_cuda_state for consumers that cannot
+ * take a PhiloxCudaState (e.g. Python). Returns 1-element int64 tensors
+ * (seed, offset, intragraph_offset); the kernel-visible values are
+ * (seed, offset + intragraph_offset), with the uint64 seed and offset
+ * reinterpreted as int64. During capture, seed and offset are aliases of
+ * the per-capture extragraph device state that replay_prologue refills on
+ * every replay; their contents are undefined until the first replay and
+ * they are only valid for that capture's lifetime. Otherwise they are
+ * device tensors holding the current values.
+ *
+ * See Note [Acquire lock when using random generators]
+ */
+std::tuple<
+    c10::intrusive_ptr<c10::TensorImpl>,
+    c10::intrusive_ptr<c10::TensorImpl>,
+    c10::intrusive_ptr<c10::TensorImpl>>

+        g = torch.Generator(device="cuda")

+        seed_t, off_t, intra_t = g.philox_cuda_state(8)

+        self.assertEqual(intra_t.item(), 0)

+            self.assertEqual(t.shape, (1,))
+        self.assertEqual(seed_t.device.type, "cuda")
+        self.assertEqual(off_t.device.type, "cuda")

+

items.author: slayton58
items.body:
They are on device in this version of the PR actually - the idea being that you no longer have to have 2 different code paths for capturing / non-capturing.

I've gone back to cpu-only (and verified DSLs can still consume RNG while captured, etc.) to match the C++ API -- I experimented a little with an optional `device=` argument, but I think that's getting too complicated, and realistically the capturing/non-capturing kernels aren't _that_ bad.
